facts.raw_span: severe bilateral pneumonia
recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history was reported
blurred vision and redness in her right eye
temporary (8-day) pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD
Relative afferent pupil defect
Central scotoma
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts (normal results)
Fluorescein Angiography (Day 30): Mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage

concepts.why: The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and had a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2.
The patient developed blurred vision and redness in her right eye, with a relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma, consistent with optic neuritis.
The patient had fluorescein angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage, consistent with retinal vasculitis.
The patient developed eye symptoms, including blurred vision and redness, in the context of a positive SARS-CoV-2 infection.
It explains the uncovered finding of central scotoma and severely impaired visual acuity.
It explains the normal cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts and the progression to severe optic nerve atrophy.

rationales.F01: Severe bilateral pneumonia is a common symptom of COVID-19.
rationales.F04: Blurred vision and redness in one eye are symptoms of optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
rationales.F06: Low visual acuity is a symptom of optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
rationales.F07: Relative afferent pupil defect is a symptom of optic neuritis.
rationales.F08: Central scotoma is a symptom of optic neuritis.
rationales.F09: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 is a diagnostic test for COVID-19.
rationales.F12: Fluorescein Angiography showing mild leakage associated with inferior peripapillary hemorrhage is a diagnostic test for retinal vasculitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of blurred vision, redness, and pain in the right eye, combined with the positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and recent close contact with a fatal case, suggest a strong link between the ophthalmological manifestations and COVID-19 infection.
